title: 1955 AHSME Problem 33
statement: Henry starts a trip when the hands of the clock are together between \(8\) a.m. and \(9\) a.m. He arrives at his destination between \(2\) p.m. and \(3\) p.m. when the hands of the clock are exactly \(180^\circ\) apart. The trip takes:

solutions.text:
At \(8{:}00,\) the hour hand is \(240^\circ\) ahead. The minute hand gains at \(5.5^\circ\) per minute, so the hands coincide \(\frac{240}{5.5}=\frac{480}{11}\) minutes after \(8.\) At \(2{:}00,\) the hour hand is \(60^\circ\) ahead. For the hands to be \(180^\circ\) apart in the relevant direction, the minute hand must gain \(240^\circ,\) again taking \(\frac{480}{11}\) minutes. The start and finish therefore have the same minute offset within their hours, exactly six hours apart.

Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: At the start, the minute hand must close a \(240^\circ\) gap at \(5.5^\circ\) per minute
Compute the corresponding time after \(2{:}00\) when the hands are opposite and compare the two offsets
